match.reason: Neither bank point teaches how to manage accounts receivable: the capital and financial account card covers international investment flows, and the efficiency ratios card covers measuring receivable turnover, not credit checks, terms, invoicing or ageing lists.

draft.title: Managing accounts receivable
card: Accounts receivable are amounts customers owe the business. A business manages them so customers pay on time and cash does not run short.
a credit check looks at whether a customer is likely to pay before credit is given. Clear terms state how many days the customer has to pay. An invoice sent promptly starts that clock sooner.
an ageing list sorts what each customer owes by how long it has been unpaid, such as 30, 60 or 90 days. It shows which overdue accounts need a reminder or a phone call first.
A spreadsheet can model options, such as the effect on cash of shorter payment terms. The business can compare choices before it picks one.
draft.remember: Check customers first, state the terms, invoice quickly, then chase the oldest debts.

a.q: What does an ageing list of accounts receivable show a business?
opts: How long each customer's debt has been unpaid
How likely a new customer is to pay in future
How many days a customer is given to pay
How much stock each customer has bought
a.why: An ageing list groups debts by how long they have been overdue, so the business knows whom to chase first. Checking if a new customer will pay is a credit check, not an ageing list.
a.clue: Think about the 30, 60 and 90 day groups.

b.q: Priya runs a timber supplier in Geelong. Some customers are paying late, and she wants to contact the ones most overdue first. Which action helps her most?
opts: Reviewing an ageing list of overdue accounts
Running a credit check on each customer now
Sending future invoices more promptly
Shortening the payment terms on the next sale
b.why: An ageing list shows which debts are oldest, so Priya knows whom to contact first. A credit check is done before credit is given, so it does not help with debts already overdue.
b.clue: Which tool sorts existing debts by how long they are unpaid?

a.best: How long each customer's debt has been unpaid

b.best: Reviewing an ageing list of overdue accounts

problems.detail: The right option is the only one that repeats the stem's word 'overdue' ('most overdue' / 'overdue accounts'). A student could match the words without knowing what an ageing list does. The clue also restates the card's definition of an ageing list, which nearly names the answer.

The why says an ageing list groups debts by how long they have been 'overdue'. The card says 'unpaid'. These differ: a debt still within its terms is unpaid but not overdue. Aligning the why with the card would avoid confusion.
